en: Now, of course, it wouldn't be an agent
without tools. So we have a tools folder and
the rule is one file per tool. So it looks
like we have a lot of tools here, but
actually EVE agents ship with some
default tools, which every agent would have
out of the box. For example, a bash tool,
which allows the agent to run
command line commands that, for example,
would allow them to write their own scripts
and then also execute them.
And if you want to disable one of these
built-in tools, and of course the
documentation will tell you which tools are
built in.
You can take a look at it and you'll see
which tools are available out of the box. If
you want to disable such a tool, you have to
create a file for it with the name of the
tool you want to disable, bash in my case,
and then import disable_tool from the Eve
library and just call and export it like
this. This will disable one of the built-in
tools and that's why I have that here.
write_file, for example, is also disabled
because my customer support agent should
neither be able to write files nor execute
random commands. Instead, I give my agent a
bunch of new commands for finding customers,
for getting the data for a customer, for
issuing refunds.
And here we'll actually also have a little
human-in-the-loop step to which I'll get
back. And all that is backed by some dummy
database, this fake store, which is in the
lib folder. Because of course, in reality,
you might be connecting your agent to a real
database, a real knowledge store,
but here for this demo, it's just some
hardcoded data, which just sets up some fake
customers to work with. Now, I did already
mention it. Human in the loop is also
something you can easily add with Eve.
You can go to a tool
and add an approval setting and, for
example, set it to always to make sure that
when the agent wants to execute that tool,
you always trigger a human approval step. So
you don't auto-execute the code, which would
be the default otherwise. The harness, the
Eve harness, would execute that tool
normally automatically. You don't don't do
that. Instead, you hand the control back to
the user who started this agent or who's
interacting with that agent, and you ask for
approval there. Now, there are different
ways of setting up that approval. Besides
always, you also get other options for
conditional approval and so on. But here,
for simplicity, I just set it to always. But
that is also supported and easy to add. It's
just one line, as you see, and you will see
it in action soon.
